title: account_id on the events table
tldr: Adds a NOT NULL account_id to events, backfills it from users, and simplifies the analytics query.

readingPlan.step: Read the migration first; the query change depends on it having run.

concerns.question: How long does ALTER TABLE events hold its lock on 50M rows?
concerns.why: ADD COLUMN NOT NULL with no default rewrites the table, and the backfill runs in the same transaction.

chapters.title: Adding and backfilling account_id
chapters.summary: One forward-only migration adds the column, backfills from users, and indexes it.
chapters.whyMatters: There is no down migration, and the backfill is unbatched inside the same lock.

sections.content: The ALTER, the UPDATE and the CREATE INDEX are all in one migration with no rollback path.

chapters.title: The analytics query drops the join
chapters.summary: eventsForAccount reads account_id directly instead of joining through users.
chapters.whyMatters: Correct only after the backfill completes; before that it silently returns nothing.

sections.content: One SQL string changes. The function signature and the db.query call are untouched.
